raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
keep fenced code examples out of qwen3 tool calls

Fixes #57541

## what happens

qwen3 models document the tool call format inside markdown fences. the parser has no fence state at all, so it reads the example XML as a real call header and emits a phantom bash tool call while swallowing most of the answer text

the reporter measured it at chunk sizes 1, 7 and 10000, all agree. on v0.29.0 and on the #56661 backport the content comes back as 59 of 149 chars and the parser reports a tool call named Bash that the model never made. i reproduced it verbatim on master at 4c6c1a4 with their CPU-only snippet, same output, no gpu needed

## the fix

a FENCE terminal on the qwen3 config plus a FENCED engine state. a fenced span runs from the first ``` to the next ``` and everything in between is emitted as plain text, streaming and non streaming

- (CONTENT, FENCE) enters FENCED and re-emits the fence itself as text
- (FENCED, FENCE) returns to CONTENT the same way
- FENCED has no tool transitions, so XML inside it can never promote
- an unterminated fence settles back to CONTENT in finish(), it never turns into a call

```xml
<tool_call>
<function=Bash>
<parameter=command>ls -la</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
```

stays exactly the text you see there. a real call right after a fenced example still parses, and backticks inside a parameter value never open a fence (TOOL_ARGS content is untouched)

## why this is not duplicating an existing PR

- search for PRs referencing #57541: 0 hits
- #56658 and #56661 fix a different case, a bare <tool_call> in prose with no fence. the reporter measured their case still broken with #56661 applied
- no open PR touches fenced example handling (157 open qwen3 and parser PRs scanned by title and by fence keyword searches)

## why engine/ changed

the vllm/parser AGENTS.md says keep model fixes in the model file and change engine/ only when the behavior is wrong for every parser. the fence semantics live in the shared state machine: FENCED is a new ParserState with a default content_events row, and finish() normalizes it like the other non-final states. without the state in engine/, the FENCE transitions cannot exist in a declarative config

## tests

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3_fenced_examples.py -q
# 8 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/ tests/parser/test_parse.py tests/parser/test_streaming.py tests/parser/test_include_reasoning.py tests/parser/test_harmony.py -q
# 4447 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/ -q -k qwen
# 88 passed, 2 skipped
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/reasoning/ -q
# 432 passed
.venv/bin/ruff check <changed files>      # clean
.venv/bin/ruff format --check <changed files>   # clean
.venv/bin/mypy <changed source files> --ignore-missing-imports   # Success
```

the new tests cover the reported case non streaming and streaming at chunk sizes 1 and 7, full text equality, the unfenced promotion staying intact, a real call after a fenced example, backticks inside a parameter value, and a fenced example right after </think>

no model evaluation was run. the change is parser level, the serving-level effect is that text the model meant as documentation stays in content instead of becoming a tool call. the reporter's serving validation showed the same defect through the full serving stack

## AI assistance

i used an AI agent to build this change, i reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable <noreply@anthropic.com>

🚀

Data point from a deployment, in support of this PR.

Tool-call conformance matrix on Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 / vLLM 0.28.0 / `qwen3_coder`, 3,600 requests with every raw generation retained. Spans were enumerated by replaying each generation through the Qwen3 parser itself rather than by pattern-matching the text: **167 spans sit inside a ``` fence**, and of the duplicate-call failures we classified, 86 are the fenced shape this PR resolves.

The other roughly three quarters are unfenced — the model quotes the markup in its reasoning block or in ordinary content. Two today-defects we hit while measuring that are filed separately and may be of interest here, since both involve the parser's treatment of quoted markup: #58227 (an unclosed `<tool_call>` opener written in prose holds the state machine in tool state through `</think>` and swallows a later genuine call) and #58228 (`finish_reason: "tool_calls"` masks a `max_tokens` truncation).

Raw generations for the fenced cases are available as fixtures if useful; they are synthetic weather/file-write calls, nothing private.

AI assistance was used for the investigation and the harness; the measurements are from my own hardware.

thanks a lot for running this matrix on your deployment and sharing the numbers @ArijitDeb, really helpful to see the fenced shape measured at scale, and the raw generations will be handy if the maintainers want fixtures

thanks @Pranjulcr7 for testing this and catching these cases, you're right, the current toggle was too simple and missed tildes, longer fence lengths, and fences inside think blocks

working on carrying delimiter and length through the parser state now so only matching fences close it, will push an update soon

pushed the update to the branch now @Pranjulcr7

carried the fence char and length through the parser engine so only matching fences close it, also added FENCED_REASONING so code inside think blocks stays in reasoning without making tool calls, and added line rules for inline backticks

added tests for all the cases and ran everything locally, let me know if it looks good on your side

Thanks @hktitof, the three reported fence cases pass at `54da2340`, including preservation of reasoning.

One regression showed up with a real tool argument containing a fenced block:

````xml
<tool_call>
<function=write_file>
<parameter=content>
```python
print(1)
```
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
````

At chunk sizes 1, 7, and whole-input, the engine sends the fence and remaining markup to content; the truncated argument converts to `{}`. This was preserved at `702e770`; tildes fail too.

Could `_handle_fence` only open fences from `CONTENT`/`REASONING`, leaving tool states alone? Checked with the same CPU engine probe and Qwen3 argument converter.

thanks for the close look @Pranjulcr7, you are right, i was opening the fence from every state and that is what clipped the argument, a fenced block inside a parameter value is argument text so it should never start a fence, now only content and reasoning open one and the tool states pass the run through as is, added a test for the backtick and tilde case at chunk sizes 1, 7 and whole input, pushed the update now

Thanks @hktitof, confirmed at `d9a2940`: both backtick and tilde blocks stay intact in the tool argument at chunk sizes 1, 7, and whole-input. The earlier fence cases still pass too. That resolves the regression I flagged in the CPU probe.

thanks for confirming the fix at d9a2940 @Pranjulcr7, good to know the fence and tilde cases stay intact at all three chunk sizes, really appreciate you rerunning the probe and the argument converter check

Tested the current head (d9a2940) on sm_120 with Qwen3.8 Flash-Next (Swift 1.5 NVFP4), `qwen3_coder` parser, 10 runs per case, same seed with and without the patch:
- fenced tool-call example, then "don't run that, run `ls -la src` instead": 10/10 with and without
- fenced example, then "explain it, don't call tools": 1/10 with and without, same 8 unwanted calls. These seem to come from `<tool_call>` written inside the reasoning rather than inside the fence, details in #58147.
- prompt asking the model to write a line with only ```bash, leave it open, then call `run_command`: the real call goes through 10/10 without the patch and 1/10 with it (9 times no tool call at all)

I know the last one is intended (`test_unterminated_content_fence_stays_content`), and my prompt asks for it explicitly, so it says nothing about how often it happens on its own. Still, Qwen3.8 does follow that pattern when asked, so the cost of this trade-off is a real call dropped without any error, and on my setup the benefit didn't show up on the phantom case.

One more thing from reading the code: at the head there's no way out of the fenced state on `</think>`, so a fence opened inside the reasoning and never closed swallows `</think>` and everything after it. Closing the fence on `</think>` passes the PR's tests plus that case, but I only checked it on CPU: https://github.com/ArtyomITA/blackwell6000-qwen3.8-flash-next/blob/61c754b12bfc92cd83fe4f25e6a709c5f687e1cd/patches/not-adopted/qwen3-parser-fence-and-reasoning-tool.diff

thanks a lot for testing the head at d9a2940 and sharing the full matrix @ArtyomITA, this is really useful
the unterminated fence case losing the real call is the intended trade off from test_unterminated_content_fence_stays_content, but you are right that the cost is a real call dropped with no error, so it is worth weighing on the gpu path
your reading of the code looks right, at head a fence opened inside reasoning and never closed swallows the reasoning close tag and everything after it, so closing the fence on that tag looks like the right direction, i only checked it on cpu so far and your patch is a helpful reference
i will run both variants on gpu against the phantom case and the reasoning path and report back here
for the phantom calls in #58147, 1/10 with and without on your setup matches what i see, so the parser change alone does not move that case
thanks again for the careful look
Thanks @hktitof! If there's any news on this, let me know.

Tried running it on my setup but couldn't get it working with the nvfp4 model bcs of kernel and hardware compatibility, so couldn't re-run the full test, on the parser side though, checked your reading on </think> on cpu and patched it so the fence closes on </think>, verified across chunk sizes 1, 7 and whole input, all 54 parser tests are green on my side
And i also pushed the update to the branch, if you get a chance to re-run your test against the new head that would be super helpful, thanks again for checking this @ArtyomITA

Re-ran it on sm_120 with e24c0af, this time with a fixed seed per request, so both runs generated the same text (59 of 60 identical). 10 runs per case:

- the 4 cases without fences: same with and without
- fenced example, then "run `ls -la src` instead": 10/10 both
- fenced example, "explain it, don't call tools": 0/10 both, same phantom calls
- open ```bash and leave it open, then call run_command: 10/10 without, 7/10 with. In the 3 lost runs the real call comes right after the open fence, so that's the trade-off you described.

One thing from the raw output that might help: every phantom call (13 across both runs) has `<tool_call>` in the middle of a line right after a backtick, like "Explain the tags: `" or "| `" inside a table, both in the reasoning and in the content. Every real call (47 to 50 per run) starts at the beginning of a line. So a rule like "a tool call only starts at the beginning of a line" would have removed all the phantoms here, the reasoning ones from #58147 included, without losing a real call. I only checked this on the outputs so far, not with a patched parser on GPU.

@ArtyomITA thanks for running it again on sm_120 with a fixed seed, first time i have real numbers instead of my own guess, and the unclosed fence case matches what i described, 7 out of 10 with the fix and the lost calls landing right after the open fence

the positional part is the useful bit, if every real call starts at the
beginning of a line and every phantom sits mid line after a backtick, then
anchoring on line start would have caught all 13 phantoms here and the
reasoning ones from #58147 too

i am not going to claim it works bcs i cannot verify it, my testing is the parser tests only, i cannot run a patched parser on sm_120 from here, and you said it is only checked on outputs so far, that is exactly that gap i also would rather not fold it into this PR, the rule is broader than fence handling and it would replace the fence logic instead of sitting next to it,so the diff becomes about where any tool call may start, a bigger call than the narrow fix this PR reviews

happy to open a follow up for the line start rule if you or someone with the hardware wants to drive it, i can write the parser change and the cases, i just cannot promise the runtime numbers

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I'm contributing three additional fence cases for #57541 to help strengthen this fix.

At `702e770`, the ordinary three-backtick example is preserved. The CPU streaming-engine probe still emits `get_weather` in these cases:

1. The example is enclosed by `~~~xml` and `~~~`.
2. A four-backtick outer fence contains a three-backtick line before the example. That shorter line should remain inside the outer fence, but the literal toggle leaves `FENCED` there.
3. The example is fenced inside reasoning. There is no corresponding fence transition from `REASONING`.

Each example contains:

```xml
<tool_call>
<function=get_weather>
<parameter=city>Paris</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
```

The results agree at chunk sizes 1, 7, and whole-input. Suggested regression coverage: both fence types, matching closing type and minimum length, line/indentation rules, and preservation of the reasoning channel. A literal toggle also risks treating inline backtick spans as block fences.

Validation used the repository's streaming engine and Qwen3 configuration, with package-level server imports bypassed and text-only feeds. No full parser-suite, special-token-ID-path, or model/server evaluation.

AI assistance was used for the investigation and CPU probes.

detail.title: fix(parser): keep fenced code examples out of qwen3 tool calls

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,561 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Fenced code examples in Qwen3 output must stay content.
+
+A fenced example documents the tool call format itself, so the XML markers
+inside it are data, not calls (vLLM issue #57541).  Markdown/CommonMark
+fence rules matter here: the closing run must use the same delimiter
+character as the opener and be at least as long, it must sit at the start
+of a line (up to three spaces of indentation), and inline code spans must
+never open a block fence.  Fences that open inside the reasoning channel
+must stay in that channel.
+"""
+
+import json
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+import pytest
+
+from tests.parser.engine.conftest import make_mock_tokenizer
+from tests.parser.engine.streaming_helpers import (
+    collect_content,
+    collect_function_name,
+    collect_tool_arguments,
+    simulate_reasoning_streaming,
+    simulate_tool_streaming,
+)
+from vllm.parser.engine.parser_engine import ParserEngine
+from vllm.parser.qwen3 import (
+    FENCE,
+    TOOL_CALL_END,
+    TOOL_CALL_START,
+    qwen3_config,
+)
+
+# Built from pieces so the literal reasoning markers survive tooling.
+THINK_START = "<" + "think" + ">"
+THINK_END = "<" + "/think" + ">"
+
+TICK = FENCE[0]
+TILDE = "~" * 3
+FOUR_TICKS = FENCE + TICK
+FOUR_TILDES = TILDE + "~"
+
+CALL = (
+    "<tool_call>\n"
+    "<function=Bash>\n"
+    "<parameter=command>ls -la</parameter>\n"
+    "</function>\n"
+    "</tool_call>\n"
+)
+
+
+def bash_tool():
+    bash = MagicMock()
+    bash.function.name = "Bash"
+    return bash
+
+
+def chunks_for(text: str, chunk_size: int | None) -> list[str]:
+    if chunk_size is None:
+        return [text]
+    return [text[i : i + chunk_size] for i in range(0, len(text), chunk_size)]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def mock_tokenizer():
+    return make_mock_tokenizer(
+        {
+            TOOL_CALL_START: 100,
+            TOOL_CALL_END: 101,
+        }
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def parser(mock_tokenizer):
+    return ParserEngine(
+        mock_tokenizer,
+        parser_engine_config=qwen3_config(thinking=False),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def thinking_parser(mock_tokenizer):
+    return ParserEngine(
+        mock_tokenizer,
+        parser_engine_config=qwen3_config(thinking=True),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def parser_with_tools(mock_tokenizer):
+    return ParserEngine(
+        mock_tokenizer,
+        tools=[bash_tool()],
+        parser_engine_config=qwen3_config(thinking=False),
+    )
+
+
+FENCED_EXAMPLE = (
+    "Here is what a tool call looks like:\n"
+    "\n" + FENCE + "xml\n" + CALL + FENCE + "\n"
+    "\n"
+    "That is the format."
+)
+
+
+class TestFencedExamplesInContent:
+    """Fenced code examples in content must stay text (vLLM issue #57541)."""
+
+    def test_fenced_example_kept_as_content(self, parser, mock_request):
+        result = parser.extract_tool_calls(FENCED_EXAMPLE, mock_request)
+
+        assert result.tools_called is False
+        assert result.tool_calls == []
+        assert result.content == FENCED_EXAMPLE
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("chunk_size", [1, 7, None])
+    def test_fenced_example_streaming_kept_as_content(
+        self, parser, mock_request, chunk_size
+    ):
+        chunks = chunks_for(FENCED_EXAMPLE, chunk_size)
+        results = simulate_tool_streaming(parser, mock_request, chunks)
+
+        assert collect_content(results) == FENCED_EXAMPLE
+        assert collect_function_name(results) is None
+
+    def test_xml_without_fence_still_promotes_tool_call(self, parser, mock_request):
+        text = (
+            "Here is what a tool call looks like:\n"
+            "\n"
+            "<tool_call>\n"
+            "<function=Bash>\n"
+            "<parameter=command>ls -la</parameter>\n"
+            "</function>\n"
+            "</tool_call>"
+        )
+        result = parser.extract_tool_calls(text, mock_request)
+
+        assert result.tools_called is True
+        assert result.tool_calls[0].function.name == "Bash"
+
+    def test_real_tool_call_after_fenced_example(self, parser, mock_request):
+        text = (
+            "Here is what a tool call looks like:\n"
+            "\n" + FENCE + "xml\n"
+            "<tool_call>\n"
+            "<function=Example>\n"
+            "<parameter=x>1</parameter>\n"
+            "</function>\n"
+            "</tool_call>\n" + FENCE + "\n"
+            "\n"
+            "Now run it for real:\n"
+            "<tool_call>\n"
+            "<function=Bash>\n"
+            "<parameter=command>pwd</parameter>\n"
+            "</function>\n"
+            "</tool_call>"
+        )
+        result = parser.extract_tool_calls(text, mock_request)
+
+        assert result.tools_called is True
+        assert len(result.tool_calls) == 1
+        assert result.tool_calls[0].function.name == "Bash"
+        args = json.loads(result.tool_calls[0].function.arguments)
+        assert args == {"command": "pwd"}
+        assert FENCE + "xml" in result.content
+
+    def test_code_fence_inside_parameter_value_is_preserved(self, parser, mock_request):
+        text = (
+            "<tool_call>\n"
+            "<function=Bash>\n"
+            "<parameter=command>echo " + TICK + "python" + TICK + " | cat</parameter>\n"
+            "</function>\n"
+            "</tool_call>"
+        )
+        result = parser.extract_tool_calls(text, mock_request)
+
+        assert result.tools_called is True
+        args = json.loads(result.tool_calls[0].function.arguments)
+        assert "python" in args["command"]
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("fence", [FENCE, TILDE])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("chunk_size", [1, 7, None])
+    def test_fenced_block_inside_parameter_value_is_preserved(
+        self, parser, mock_request, fence, chunk_size
+    ):
+        text = (
+            "<tool_call>\n"
+            "<function=write_file>\n"
+            "<parameter=content>\n" + fence + "python\n"
+            "print(1)\n" + fence + "\n"
+            "</parameter>\n"
+            "</function>\n"
+            "</tool_call>"
+        )
+        results = simulate_tool_streaming(
+            parser, mock_request, chunks_for(text, chunk_size)
+        )
+
+        assert "print(1)" in collect_tool_arguments(results)
+
+    def test_fenced_example_after_think_end(self, thinking_parser, mock_request):
+        fenced = FENCE + "xml\ncode\n" + FENCE + "\n"
+        text = THINK_START + "\nreasoning here\n" + THINK_END + "\n" + fenced
+        result = thinking_parser.extract_tool_calls(text, mock_request)
+
+        assert result.tools_called is False
+        assert result.tool_calls == []
+        assert result.content == "\n" + fenced
+
+    def test_streaming_matches_non_streaming(self, parser, mock_request):
+        chunks = chunks_for(FENCED_EXAMPLE, 7)
+        results = simulate_tool_streaming(parser, mock_request, chunks)
+        assert collect_content(results) == FENCED_EXAMPLE
+        assert collect_function_name(results) is None
+
+
+class TestFenceDelimiters:
+    """Both backtick and tilde fences are recognized, and they do not mix."""
+
+    def test_tilde_fence_kept_as_content(self, parser, mock_request):
+        text = "Example:\n" + TILDE + "xml\n" + CALL + TILDE + "\ndone"
+        result = parser.extract_tool_calls(text, mock_request)
+
+        assert result.tools_called is False
+        assert result.content == text
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("chunk_size", [1, 7, None])
+    def test_tilde_fence_streaming_kept_as_content(
+        self, parser, mock_request, chunk_size
+    ):

Data point from a deployment, in support of this PR.

Tool-call conformance matrix on Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 / vLLM 0.28.0 / `qwen3_coder`, 3,600 requests with every raw generation retained. Spans were enumerated by replaying each generation through the Qwen3 parser itself rather than by pattern-matching the text: **167 spans sit inside a ``` fence**, and of the duplicate-call failures we classified, 86 are the fenced shape this PR resolves.

The other roughly three quarters are unfenced — the model quotes the markup in its reasoning block or in ordinary content. Two today-defects we hit while measuring that are filed separately and may be of interest here, since both involve the parser's treatment of quoted markup: #58227 (an unclosed `<tool_call>` opener written in prose holds the state machine in tool state through `</think>` and swallows a later genuine call) and #58228 (`finish_reason: "tool_calls"` masks a `max_tokens` truncation).

Raw generations for the fenced cases are available as fixtures if useful; they are synthetic weather/file-write calls, nothing private.

AI assistance was used for the investigation and the harness; the measurements are from my own hardware.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I'm contributing three additional fence cases for #57541 to help strengthen this fix.

At `702e770`, the ordinary three-backtick example is preserved. The CPU streaming-engine probe still emits `get_weather` in these cases:

1. The example is enclosed by `~~~xml` and `~~~`.
2. A four-backtick outer fence contains a three-backtick line before the example. That shorter line should remain inside the outer fence, but the literal toggle leaves `FENCED` there.
3. The example is fenced inside reasoning. There is no corresponding fence transition from `REASONING`.

Each example contains:

```xml
<tool_call>
<function=get_weather>
<parameter=city>Paris</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
```

The results agree at chunk sizes 1, 7, and whole-input. Suggested regression coverage: both fence types, matching closing type and minimum length, line/indentation rules, and preservation of the reasoning channel. A literal toggle also risks treating inline backtick spans as block fences.

Validation used the repository's streaming engine and Qwen3 configuration, with package-level server imports bypassed and text-only feeds. No full parser-suite, special-token-ID-path, or model/server evaluation.

AI assistance was used for the investigation and CPU probes.
